properties.name: An objection aimed at an inference step (an undercutter) is read against that step: the step reads contested or defeated, and the read-back lists it
properties.source: @ajs, 2026-10-18: "Capture the shortcomings (gaps) from the trial" (cogito trial, fact:the-cogito-trial-ran-on-flo2-io-and-its-friction-names-what-a-line-of-reasoning-lacks-2026-10-18)
properties.statement:
An objection can attack the STEP itself (its warrant or rule) rather than a premise or the conclusion. Such an objection is read against the step: while it stands, the step reads contested; when it holds unanswered, the step is defeated and does not support its conclusion; reasoning_report lists it under the step; a reply to it reinstates the step.
Observed in the cogito trial (2026-10-18, flo2.io 989598dd02246a81, reflow2 0.87.0), reported by the designer: a CONTRADICTS edge into inf:cogito-as-intuition was stored, and the step still read `holds`, unlisted. The workaround was to write each challenged warrant as a taken-as-given premise for the objection to aim at, which put four extra claims in the design.
This is idea (b), "an objection against a step", of dec:idea-what-reflow2-takes-from-the-argumentation-frameworks, now with a measured need.
